original_question: Consider a balanced excited random walk, meaning that for every site z, direction e, and visit number i one has ω(z,e,i) = ω(z,-e,i), so the local cookies do not create directional bias. Under uniform ellipticity and either i.i.d. or stationary-and-ergodic cookie environments, is every such walk recurrent in dimension 2 and transient in dimensions d >= 3?
target_in_paper: Section 3.2, Remark and Problem 3.22 (“d ≥ 2, balanced ERW”), read together with Definition 3.1 for the meaning of recurrence/transience and Section 1 for the ERW model and the assumptions (IID), (SE), and (UEL). ([sites.math.duke.edu](https://sites.math.duke.edu/~rtd/readS18/KosZer.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft captures the right open problem: the paper asks about a balanced excited random walk, under uniform ellipticity and either i.i.d. or stationary-and-ergodic cookie environments, and whether the expected dimension dichotomy is recurrence in d = 2 versus transience in d ≥ 3. Your symmetry condition ω(z,e,i) = ω(z,-e,i) is exactly the balance condition used in the paper. ([sites.math.duke.edu](https://sites.math.duke.edu/~rtd/readS18/KosZer.pdf))

Balance is formulated as a property of the environment law P: P-a.s., ω(z,e,i) = ω(z,-e,i) for every z in Z^d, e in E, and i in N. Your draft states the symmetry pointwise but omits the P-a.s. quantifier and the role of P. ([sites.math.duke.edu](https://sites.math.duke.edu/~rtd/readS18/KosZer.pdf))

refined_question: Let P be a probability law on cookie environments Ω = M_E^{Z^d×N}, where E = {±e_j : 1 ≤ j ≤ d}, and let X = (X_n)_{n≥0} be the corresponding nearest-neighbor excited random walk on Z^d started at 0 under the averaged law P0. Assume d ≥ 2, that P satisfies either (IID) or (SE), and that P is uniformly elliptic in the sense that there exists κ > 0 such that P-a.s. ω(z,e,i) ≥ κ for all z in Z^d, e in E, and i in N. Suppose moreover that P is balanced, i.e. P-a.s. ω(z,e,i) = ω(z,-e,i) for every z in Z^d, e in E, and i in N. Must X be recurrent when d = 2, in the sense that every site of Z^d is visited infinitely often P0-a.s., and transient when d ≥ 3, in the sense that no site is visited infinitely often (equivalently, |X_n| → ∞) P0-a.s.? ([sites.math.duke.edu](https://sites.math.duke.edu/~rtd/readS18/KosZer.pdf))
justification: This draft is targeting the paper’s later open problem on balanced excited random walks, not Conjecture 1.1 / Proposition 1.2 / Theorem 1.3. Section 1 defines the ERW model, the environment law P, and the assumptions (IID), (SE), and (UEL); Definition 3.1 defines recurrence and transience; and Section 3.2 then states Remark and Problem 3.22, which asks whether every balanced ERW satisfying (IID) (or (SE)) and (UEL) is recurrent in d = 2 and transient in d ≥ 3. The surrounding lines also explain the motivation from the M(d1,d2)-RW examples and record a partial d ≥ 3 finite-return-to-0 result under a stronger finite-cookie-type assumption. ([sites.math.duke.edu](https://sites.math.duke.edu/~rtd/readS18/KosZer.pdf))
